title: The Summer of the Crescent Cove
premise: Ulyana Quintana has spent ten years writing other people's truths while burying her own — including the sentence she never said to Theo Marchetti, the boy she left behind in Crescent Cove when duty called her to the city. Now a ghostwriting contract drags her back home, where her family's failing bakery lease expires at summer's end and her mother expects her to sign it away. To survive the reunion without confessing her secret career, Ulyana recruits Theo — now the town's beloved baker and her rival's confidant — as a fake date. But the pretense cracks by dessert, and as the lease deadline looms, Ulyana must choose between the inheritance of silence her family demands and the life, love, and voice she abandoned. In the end, she says the rehearsed sentence aloud, signs nothing, and claims both the bakery and Theo on her own terms.
about_author: Marguerite Eriksen is the pen name of a former pastry chef who traded early mornings at a seaside bakery for late nights writing love stories set in small coastal towns. She lives within walking distance of the ocean and believes every good romance deserves a second proofing.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ghostwriter Ulyana Quintana returns to Crescent Cove under cover of a family visit, secretly contracted to write a rival author's memoir that may expose the town. Her mother announces the bakery lease expires in six weeks and pressures her to let it go. The emotional beat: dread braided with homesickness, as Ulyana rehearses evasions like old recipes.

chapters.title: The Fake Date Clause
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ulyana and Theo. To deflect her aunt's matchmaking at the reunion, Ulyana asks Theo Marchetti — her first love, now the cove's baker — to pose as her boyfriend. He agrees with unsettling ease. Between passed platters and pointed questions, old intimacy resurfaces. The beat: giddy denial; both pretend the electricity is part of the act.

chapters.title: What the Memoir Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV deepens as he discovers Ulyana is ghostwriting the memoir that could ruin his bakery's future — and realizes their 'fake' date was dessert-sweet and devastatingly real. Confronted at the dock, Ulyana admits everything except the one sentence she's rehearsed for a decade. The beat: betrayal and raw honesty colliding at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the lease's final day, Ulyana refuses to sign away the bakery, exposes her ghostwriting arrangement to reclaim her own name, and finally speaks the rehearsed sentence to Theo: that she has loved him in every tense but present, until now. The beat: release and renewal — love claimed against duty, identity rewritten in her own hand.
